Contacts and email-pattern resolution

Civic Operator's "not published" flag means it could not cite a public page for a row, not that the address is missing. So the useful operation is conformance: each unsourced address is checked against the pattern its domain's sourced addresses establish. Conforming is corroboration. Deviating is the row worth a human minute before it enters a sequence. Inferred addresses, where nothing was published at all, are labelled as inferred and never merged into the verified column.

How the score is computed

Two scores, both on real inputs only. Move the weights and every table updates; they are saved with your data so the model you ship is the model you tuned.

1 · State opportunity index

A state is attractive when it has money that has not moved yet, when CMS itself judged its rural need to be high, and when it is visibly active in your feed.

Remainder — money still to be awarded

remainder = FY26 award − observed first-tier subawards. A subtraction, not an opinion. Kentucky has moved about 9.6% of its award across 19 recipients; Idaho and Missouri have no observed first-tier movement at all, so every dollar is still ahead of them. States with no observation are scored as unmoved and flagged, because absence of a record is not evidence of absence of an award.

Discretionary intensity — CMS's own rural-need score

Public Law 119-21 splits the $10B annual pool in half: 50% divided equally among approved states ($100M each), 50% allocated by CMS on rurality, rural health system condition, state policy actions, and expected impact. So award − $100,000,000 is CMS's scoring of that state, denominated in dollars. Texas scores $181.3M, New Jersey $47.3M — a 3.8× spread that required no modelling and no proxy. This is the single most useful derived quantity in the system and it comes free with the award table.

Signal activity and reachability

Distinct RHTP solicitations observed for the state across your stored editions, and the share of its contacts that carry a public source. Both grow as you add briefings.

2 · Target score

Per organization, five factors, each on [0,1]:

  • ICP fit — segment mapped to the tiering in the ICP matrix. Tier 1 (CBO, perinatal, ABA, state associations) scores 1.0; FQHC and GOV 0.8; rural hospitals 0.6; school districts and universities 0.35.
  • State opportunity — the SOI above, normalised.
  • Reach — best contact verification level, plus a bonus when both an economic buyer and a champion are mapped, because a named champion is the actual entry point and a buyer alone is a cold call with a title.
  • Urgency — days to the nearest deadline attached to that organization's opportunity. Peaks in the 14–150 day band. Under 7 days you are too late to shape an application; past 240 days nobody is deciding yet.
  • Role fit — whether the governing solicitation permits subgrants or partnerships, extracted from the notice text. Idaho's school-based hub RFA explicitly allows districts to subgrant to community organizations, which is Avocado's slot exactly.

Expected value multiplies the score by the segment ACV midpoint from the ICP matrix and discounts by the segment's typical cycle length at 35% a year, so a $400K state deal on a 12-month cycle does not automatically outrank a $37.5K CBO deal that closes in four months.

Weights

What this is not

There is no trained model in this file, deliberately. A gradient-boosted ranker needs labelled history — solicitations with known applicants and known winners — and RHTP has produced exactly one round of first-tier awards so far. Training on that would produce a model fit to nineteen Kentucky recipients and dressed up as intelligence.

What runs here is a transparent weighted model over real observed quantities. Every score decomposes into named contributions you can read and argue with. When the award history exists — roughly two more subaward cycles, or a backfill across adjacent assistance listings 93.505, 93.926 and 93.994 — the learned ranker in the companion spec drops into the same interface and the scoring tab becomes its explanation rather than its replacement.

Saying so is not a limitation to hide. A CEO who is told "the model learned this" about a number that came from nineteen data points will stop trusting the next thing you show him.

Live refresh

The States tab tries to read current subaward records directly from the USAspending API. If your browser blocks that request, run fetch_live.py from the source bundle and drop the resulting JSON on the Add-briefing tab — same result, one extra step. The dashboard never silently substitutes stale data for live data; the indicator in the header always shows which you are looking at.

Handling

Contact rows are MNDA-covered and contain named individuals at public agencies and private organizations. Everything stays in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent to any server, including by the PDF parser, which runs client-side.
